title: SN 1987A — the star Earth felt before it saw

segments.en: In nineteen eighty-seven, Earth felt a star explode, hours before anyone could see it.
segments.en_cap: In 1987, Earth felt | a star explode, | hours before anyone | could see it.

segments.en: It burned hydrogen for some ten million years, and silicon for only about two weeks, down to an iron core the size of Earth.
segments.en_cap: It burned hydrogen | for ~10 million years, | and silicon for only | about 2 weeks, | down to an iron core | the size of Earth.

segments.en: Iron can't burn. In under a second, the core collapsed to the size of a city, and fired out ten to the fifty-eight neutrinos.
segments.en_cap: Iron can't burn. | In under a second, | the core collapsed | to the size of a city, | and fired out | ten to the fifty-eight | neutrinos.

segments.en: They flew straight through the star. The shockwave took about two hours to reach the surface.
segments.en_cap: They flew straight | through the star. | The shockwave took | about 2 hours | to reach the surface.

segments.en: A hundred and sixty-eight thousand years later, they came up through more than four thousand kilometers of rock, into a water tank in Japan. It caught twelve.

segments.en: Hours later came the light: the first supernova seen by eye since sixteen-oh-four. Then its debris hit a ring the star had shed twenty thousand years before.

segments.en: In twenty twenty-four, Webb found its likely heart: a neutron star, hidden in the dust. The one whose neutrinos got here first.
